input.prompt: Create one static 16:9 visual design reference for a private research memory-palace room viewer, not a real reconstruction and not an official brand page. Two adjacent panels show the SAME compact teal bedroom composition and SAME viewpoint: left large primary view uses detailed photo-like textured surfaces; right smaller alternate view uses fine ordered square dithered matrix marks on the identical continuous furniture geometry. Teal walls, a bed with pillows and wooden headboard, distinct bedside storage and a lamp are illustrative placeholders only; do not represent them as detected facts. Keep furniture separate and grounded, no cross-object connecting triangles, no extra rooms, no dramatic invented geometry. Dark charcoal surrounding canvas, generous negative space, restrained square UI primitives. Minimal compact controls: Surfaces / Matrix, View reset, Sources & details. One quiet badge reads 'Scan-assisted · unreviewed'; a subtle evidence cue distinguishes inferred closure from supplied surfaces using hollow marks, not color alone. Stable selected-object outline and a discreet accessible object-list affordance. Typeface feel: Space Grotesk and IBM Plex Sans/Mono, readable high-contrast labels and visible keyboard focus, no tiny dashboard telemetry, no marketing copy. No animation, no glow, no photographic fabrication claims, no loading progress fiction. Include a small 'Design reference — not source evidence' label. This image guides materials, composition and control hierarchy only; implementation must use real source-bound geometry, never copy this invented room layout.
